title: Synthesis brief: Roadmap alignment prep (Product / Eng / Applied ML) — Mila's scratchpad
content:
Purpose: rapid prep notes for the cross-functional roadmap alignment sync (Product, Eng, Applied ML). This is a working scratchpad — use as my speaking notes, quick references, and action-item tracker post-meeting.

Meeting goals (what I want to accomplish in 30–45m):
- Get explicit agreement on the top-3 prioritized roadmap bets for next 8 weeks (Q2 sprint window).
- Ensure applied-ML has the evaluation/guardrail plan for any model changes; Eng has a rollout policy and perf SLOs; Product signs off on customer-impact metrics.
- Surface any blocking infra or infra-cost constraints so we can decide to defer or scope down.

Context summary (one-liners to orient folks):
- Product asks: reduce median and 95th-token latency for hosted text-generation by 20% for standard prompts without regressing quality beyond 2% on key eval set. This drives adoption for chat use-cases.
- Eng constraints: limited additional GPU headroom this quarter, autoscaling knobs may add cost; rollout needs canary + automated fallback.
- Applied ML: model family candidates include: 1) quantized 8-bit variant of current v2, 2) smaller distilled checkpoint with tuned prompts, 3) reconfigured KV-cache sharding. Each has different perf/quality/cost tradeoffs.

Key decision axes (use as rubric during discussion):
- Latency improvement (median / 95th / tail)
- Quality delta on proprietary evals (pass/fail threshold)
- Additional infra cost ($ / 1000 requests) and capacity needs
- Operational complexity (rollout, observability, debugability)
- Time-to-ship (engineering + evaluation effort)

Proposed prioritized bets (my recommendation going into the meeting):
1) Short term (4–6 weeks): Ship 8-bit quantized variant behind opt-in flag + canary 5% traffic. Requires eval pass on prompt suite and small infra change to inference config. Rationale: highest upside vs dev effort.
2) Medium (6–12 weeks): Launch a tuned-distilled variant for chat-lite customers (dramatically lower cost). Only if eval shows <=3% quality delta.
3) Stretch (12+ weeks): Explore KV-cache sharding improvements (requires runtime changes and infra testing). Good long-term cost/latency wins but higher risk.

Risks / counters (call these out during sync):
- Quantization could produce subtle hallucination patterns on long-context prompts; applied-ML must own targeted evals (along with human spot checks) before we widen rollout.
- Distillation may break structured-output behaviour used by some internal customers — need per-route gating.
- KV-cache work will require coordination with Dedicated team for reserved capacity tests; schedule slip possible.

Concrete eval & rollout checklist (assigned):
- Applied ML: run 2,000-prompt regression suite + humans-on-edge checks for quantized v2; produce pass/fail by Mar 30. (Owner: Nina Patel; target: 2026-03-30)
- Eng: add opt-in config and canary routing for quantized model; include tracing hooks and token-level latency metrics. Small infra change PR + rollout playbook. (Owner: Ravi Gupta; target: 2026-04-05)
- Product/PM: define top-3 customer segments and 2 acceptance metrics per segment for A/B (Owner: Eli Park; target: 2026-03-26)
- SRE/Observability: alert thresholds for increased error rates and token-quality regressions; make sample streamer for failed requests. (Owner: TBD; ask SRE in meeting)

Quick numbers to cite in sync:
- Current median token latency for hosted standard prompts: ~42ms/token (baseline). Goal: ~34ms/token.
- Current estimated infra cost per 1k requests (standard chat profile): $0.72. Target: reduce relative cost by 15% on canary traffic.
- Eval tolerance: no more than 2% absolute drop on 'topline-quality' eval; no more than 4% drop on any critical route.

Open questions to surface (I want answers/commitments):
- Can Eng commit a 2-week dev cycle for the opt-in + canary infra work (Ravi)? If not, what's the realistic timeline?
- Will Applied ML accept the human review cadence proposed (weekly spot checks for 4 weeks post-canary)?
- Do we have capacity for a 5% canary across EU + US regions simultaneously? If not, propose sequential region rollouts.
- Are there contractual/customer SLAs that prevent routing certain customers to quantized variants? (Product to list blocked customers)

Notes-to-self: quick script and talking points
- Start: "We have three tractable bets; I want to decide which two we push this quarter and which we tuck. Goal is to reduce latency while keeping quality -> here is a pragmatic canary-first approach."
- Emphasize: keep product-metrics front-and-center (conversion/retention proxies), not just raw latency.
- If pushback on risk: propose extended canary (5%->20% over 2 weeks) with automatic rollback trigger on quality alerts.

Post-meeting action item template (I'll copy/paste into follow-up):
- Action: <short description> | Owner: <name> | Due: <YYYY-MM-DD> | Blockers: <short> | Status: todo/in-progress/done

Draft follow-ups I will send after sync (fill in during meeting):
- One-paragraph decision summary with chosen bets and rationale.
- Shared action-item tracker (I'll create a Google Sheet and link).
- Ask Applied ML for preliminary regression artifacts (Jupyter notebook + summary CSV).
- Request Eng PR link + staging rollout window in 48 hours.

Potential blockers I should raise proactively:
- If SRE cannot add the necessary tracing within 2 weeks, we need to reduce canary size and extend hold windows.
- If we discover a customer with strict SLA/no-quantized routing, Product must provide a list by end of week.

My planned follow-ups in next 72h (personal checklist):
- Create the post-meeting Google Sheet (action tracker) and add owners/targets. (Due: 2026-03-21)
- Ping SRE on availability for tracing work and include in the meeting agenda. (Done/ask during sync)
- Draft the one-paragraph summary email, leave placeholders for decisions. (Due: same day)

Capturing quick links to reference during the call:
- Perf benchmark dashboard (internal): dashboards.redwood/perf/hosted-latency (tell folks to open)
- Eval suite repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/main/regressions
- Existing runtime PR with batching improvements: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-runtime/pull/395

Final thought to seed conversation: "If we can accept a very small, monitored quality delta for 5% traffic and show meaningful latency/cost wins, that begins to open up a self-serve growth motion for chat use-cases while buying us time to do higher-risk runtime refactors."

-- end of scratchpad --

(Will update this doc live during the sync and then save a cleaned 'decisions + actions' note to Drive in the recommended path: shared_drives/product/roadmap/notes/)
